docs.text: OGC Records and STAC ¶ OGCRecord is supplied by pystac-ext-ogc-record . It provides PySTAC-compatible links, assets, and metadata APIs while retaining OGC Record serialization. Object compatibility does not imply document equivalence ¶ An OGC Record may describe a service without geometry or a STAC temporal extent. OGC time and STAC datetime fields are separate concepts. Storing an OGC Record must not invent an observation time or move OGC fields to fit a STAC document. The extension's explicit to_stac_item() conversion requires a STAC temporal extent. This library does not call that method during storage. Relationship to stac-geoparquet ¶ stac-geoparquet provides STAC-oriented conversion and shares the underlying Arrow, WKB, and GeoParquet building blocks. It is credited in the repository's NOTICE . This library's contract additionally keeps the full OGC payload and storage-only membership separate from the query columns. These are local format choices; an OGC Records Parquet file is not automatically a STAC-GeoParquet document. The implementation depends directly on PySTAC, PyArrow, Shapely, and PyProj. It does not import or patch stac-geoparquet internals. Membership is an external association ¶ A catalog description explains a collection. It does not identify which rows belong to it. The nullable __collection_id column stores that association explicitly, independently of record IDs and of any collection member in the original document. This permits duplicate IDs across collections and unknown membership. It also means an old file containing only descriptions cannot reveal lost memberships without an external source. Validation responsibilities ¶ The package checks storage types, JSON representability, projection safety, and format compatibility. OGC conformance and profile validation belong to the caller. OGCRecord.validate() needs an explicitly supplied OGC validator; the storage pipeline does not perform that validation automatically. See collection membership for practical usage.

docs.text: Preservation and projections ¶ A record can contain deeply nested, heterogeneous metadata that does not fit a single useful query schema. The library therefore stores two representations: the serialized record and a selected set of typed Arrow columns. The document is authoritative ¶ __record_json stores OGCRecord.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) . Readers reconstruct records from this payload through OGCRecord.from_dict() . They do not reconstruct documents from query columns. This separation permits a field to appear only in later records or have different shapes across records without requiring it to be an Arrow column. An explicit projection can select the fields your service needs. Changing a query column does not edit the record. To change the document, recover the OGCRecord , use its APIs, and serialize it again. Preservation starts at the PySTAC boundary ¶ The package preserves the extension's serialized values, not raw source bytes. PySTAC handles record construction, links, assets, and timestamp normalization. For example, timestamps are normalized to UTC whole seconds, and absent links may become an empty list. The storage layer validates that the resulting document contains finite JSON values and string keys. It rejects tuples and non-string keys instead of allowing the JSON encoder to silently coerce them. Decoding rejects duplicate keys. Validation checks existing containers without making a second deep copy. Relative hrefs are serialized without transformation. Source self links, when present, are included. An independent recovered record can be edited without changing the file or another recovered record. Query geometry and document geometry have different roles ¶ The binary geometry column supports spatial tools. Its bbox is derived from geometry and provides a two-dimensional covering. The original serialized geometry and bbox remain in the payload, including foreign geometry members and a possible six-coordinate bbox. Null and empty geometries have a null covering. An empty geometry still has a WKB representation; a null geometry does not. Predictability has a storage cost ¶ Each batch uses the same projection schema. Conversion consumes input once, in order, and does not perform full-file schema inference or disk-backed schema unification. This makes projection choices explicit. The payload adds storage alongside the columns. Batching limits the number of records processed together, but is not a fixed memory bound: document size and Arrow allocations also matter. No throughput or compression benchmark is promised by the API. See projection how-to and storage reference .

docs.text: Store collection membership ¶ Supply catalog descriptions and per-row memberships separately. Descriptions alone do not establish membership. from pystac.extensions.ogc_record import OGCRecord from ogc_records_parquet import ( read_collection_ids, read_collections, read_parquet, records_to_arrow, to_parquet, ) records = [ OGCRecord(id="shared-id", properties={"title": "Application"}), OGCRecord(id="shared-id", properties={"title": "Unclassified"}), ] catalogs = { "applications": { "id": "applications", "type": "Collection", "links": [], "itemType": "record", }, } memberships = ["applications", None] to_parquet( records_to_arrow(records, collections=catalogs, collection_ids=memberships), "collections.parquet", ) assert read_collections("collections.parquet") == catalogs assert list(read_collection_ids("collections.parquet")) == memberships assert [record.id for record in read_parquet("collections.parquet")] == [ "shared-id", "shared-id" ] Align membership with rows ¶ Provide exactly one membership per record, in the same order. Use a non-empty string for known membership and None for unknown membership. Keep both iterables aligned when generating them lazily. Pair separately read records and memberships only when they represent the same rows in the same order. Length mismatches and invalid membership values fail during consumption. Duplicate record identifiers are allowed because association is positional. Preserve the original record ¶ __collection_id is storage-only membership. It does not replace or insert the record's collection field. Catalog descriptions are serialized into metadata during records_to_arrow() ; later changes to the supplied dictionaries do not change that snapshot. The library requires catalog values to be JSON objects. It does not validate catalog schemas, match their IDs to mapping keys, or require membership IDs to have descriptions. For older files, see migration .

docs.text: Import and export records ¶ Use PySTAC for individual JSON documents. Install the package in your local checkout before running these examples from the repository root. For shell-based imports from local files or remote URLs, see the command-line interface . Import an example file ¶ from pathlib import Path from pystac.extensions.ogc_record import OGCRecord from ogc_records_parquet import read_parquet, records_to_arrow, to_parquet source = Path( "examples/ogc-records/hazard-mapping/records/diachronic-flood-detection.json" ) record = OGCRecord.from_file(source) to_parquet(records_to_arrow([record]), "imported.parquet") restored = next(read_parquet("imported.parquet")) assert restored.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) == record.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) restored.save_object(dest_href="exported-record.json") from_file() assigns a self link to the source file. Storage includes that link and preserves relative hrefs without rewriting them. Read without adding a source self link ¶ Use the following alternative when only links present in the document should be retained: from pystac import StacIO from pystac.extensions.ogc_record import OGCRecord document = StacIO.default().read_json( "examples/ogc-records/hazard-mapping/records/diachronic-flood-detection.json" ) record = OGCRecord.from_dict(document) For in-memory dictionaries, likewise call OGCRecord.from_dict(document) before records_to_arrow() . Select records from arrays or FeatureCollections in the calling application. The package does not provide JSON container or NDJSON readers. Edit links and assets ¶ Use the record's PySTAC APIs before storing it again: from pystac import Asset, Link from pystac.extensions.ogc_record import OGCRecord from ogc_records_parquet import records_to_arrow, to_parquet record = OGCRecord(id="workflow", properties={"title": "Flood workflow"}) record.add_link(Link("related", "../related.json")) record.add_asset("workflow", Asset("./workflow.cwl", roles=["data"])) to_parquet(records_to_arrow([record]), "workflow.parquet") The asset href is stored as supplied; storage does not read or execute the CWL document. See normalization and preservation for timestamp and optional-field behavior.

docs.text: Migrate existing applications and files ¶ Replace the dictionary API ¶ The current API accepts OGCRecord instances. Replace direct dictionary inputs with OGCRecord.from_dict(document) . Returned values are also OGCRecord instances; use to_dict() at JSON boundaries. The old ogc_records_parquet.json module and its read_json , read_ndjson , and write_ndjson helpers have been removed. Use PySTAC file APIs for individual documents and handle container selection or NDJSON framing in your application. Check normalization expectations ¶ Compare records against OGCRecord.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) . The extension normalizes metadata timestamps and STAC temporal fields to UTC whole seconds, including nested metadata timestamps, and normalizes some optional fields. Byte identity, fractional timestamp precision, and every missing-versus-null distinction are not preserved. These parsing rules also apply when reading legacy stored payloads. Rewrite a legacy file ¶ Readers accept storage formats 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 . Legacy membership reads as None for every row. To rewrite a legacy file with the current format, run the following in a directory containing legacy.parquet : from ogc_records_parquet import ( read_collection_ids, read_collections, read_parquet, records_to_arrow, to_parquet, ) records = list(read_parquet("legacy.parquet")) catalogs = read_collections("legacy.parquet") to_parquet( records_to_arrow(records, collections=catalogs), "migrated.parquet", ) assert list(read_collection_ids("migrated.parquet")) == [None] * len(records) assert [record.to_dict() for record in read_parquet("migrated.parquet")] == [ record.to_dict() for record in records ] If a trustworthy external source provides memberships, pass its aligned iterable as collection_ids= to records_to_arrow() . Do not infer membership from titles, duplicate record IDs, or catalog descriptions alone. Reserializing uses the default query projections unless you explicitly supply a schema. Preserve any application-specific projections by passing that schema. Merely copying an existing Arrow stream through to_parquet() preserves its format version; it does not upgrade the stream. See format compatibility for version details.

docs.text: Project and filter records ¶ Supply an Arrow schema when you need query columns beyond the defaults. Use dot-separated object paths as field names. Select the columns ¶ This complete example builds two records and projects their service type, title, and update time: import pyarrow as pa import pyarrow.compute as pc from pystac.extensions.ogc_record import OGCRecord from ogc_records_parquet import arrow_to_records, records_to_arrow records = [ OGCRecord( id="flood", properties={ "type": "service", "title": "Flood mapping", "updated": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", }, ), OGCRecord(id="archive", properties={"type": "dataset", "title": "Archive"}), ] schema = pa.schema([ pa.field("id", pa.string(), nullable=False), pa.field("properties.type", pa.string()), pa.field("properties.title", pa.string()), pa.field("properties.updated", pa.timestamp("us", tz="UTC")), ]) table = records_to_arrow(records, schema=schema, batch_size=1).read_all() assert table["properties.updated"].null_count == 1 selected = table.filter(pc.equal(table["properties.type"], "service")) restored = list(arrow_to_records(selected)) assert [record.id for record in restored] == ["flood"] assert restored[0].to_dict() == records[0].to_dict() Keep __record_json and the format metadata when passing results back to arrow_to_records() . Filtering full rows retains these. Selecting only query columns prevents record reconstruction. Project nested lists ¶ An explicit list/struct type can project a whole list: schema = pa.schema([ pa.field("id", pa.string()), pa.field("links", pa.list_(pa.struct([ pa.field("href", pa.string()), pa.field("rel", pa.string()), pa.field("type", pa.string()), ]))), ]) table = records_to_arrow(records, schema=schema).read_all() assert table.num_rows == 2 Paths do not traverse list elements or escape literal dots in object keys. Handle those cases in the calling application. Missing paths project as null; use nullable=False to reject them. Unsafe numeric casts fail when the stream is consumed. Query with SQL ¶ Dotted names are literal column names. In DuckDB, quote them: SELECT id, "properties.title" FROM read_parquet('records.parquet') WHERE "properties.type" = 'service'; SQL execution is outside this package. The repository notebook at notebooks/query_ogc_records.ipynb demonstrates collection filtering and CQL2 translation with pygeofilter-duckdb==0.2.0 . Install its dependencies from the checkout: python -m pip install -e ".[notebook]" Open the notebook in a notebook-capable editor using that Python environment. It writes notebooks/output/ogc-records.parquet . See the storage reference for the reserved columns.

docs.text: Project Records into a lazy Arrow stream with PySTAC-serialized payloads. Record and membership iterables are consumed only when the reader is advanced. Records are serialized at that time, so changes made before consumption are visible. Collection descriptions are instead validated and serialized immediately. The input records and descriptions are not modified. Each row retains the document produced by OGCRecord.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) , including self links and unmodified relative hrefs. PySTAC normalization applies before storage; original JSON bytes and pre-normalization timestamp precision are not preserved. Null geometry and records without STAC temporal fields are supported. Non-null geometry must already use CRS84 longitude/latitude. Parameters: records ( Iterable [ OGCRecord ] ) – One-pass iterable of OGCRecord objects in source order. docs.text: Decode OGCRecord objects from a library-produced Arrow stream. Stored payloads are authoritative: editing query or membership columns does not edit the exported records. Decoding follows OGCRecord.from_dict() , including its normalization rules for legacy payloads. No OGC profile validation is performed. docs.text: Command-line interface ¶ Install the optional CLI dependencies: pip install 'ogc-records-parquet[cli]' ogc-records-parquet --help Import records ¶ Pass one or more individual OGC Record JSON documents and a destination: ogc-records-parquet \ examples/ogc-records/hazard-mapping/records/diachronic-flood-detection.json \ --output output/records.parquet Inputs may mix local paths with HTTP, HTTPS, file:// , and oci:// URLs. Records retain their argument order. Each source must contain one record; arrays, FeatureCollections, and NDJSON are not supported. The CLI parses sources with PySTAC's OGCRecord.from_dict() , without adding a source self link. The command loads all records before writing, creates missing output directories, and overwrites an existing destination. It does not provide streaming ingestion, filtering, or JSON export. Use the Python API for those workflows. Options and authentication ¶ Option Environment variable Behavior --output PATH — Required destination GeoParquet file. --oauth2-bearer TOKEN OAUTH2_BEARER Bearer token for HTTP and HTTPS requests. --oci-hostname HOST OCI_HOSTNAME Registry host for explicit credentials. --oci-username USER OCI_USERNAME Registry username. --oci-password PASSWORD OCI_PASSWORD Registry password. --authfile PATH REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE Registry credentials file. --help — Show usage and exit. Explicit options take precedence over their environment variables. All three OCI credential options must be supplied to add credentials for the specified host. A credentials file can also supply registry authentication. If it does not exist, the command starts with empty credentials before adding explicit credentials. The default credentials path is resolved when the command runs: Linux with a nonempty XDG_RUNTIME_DIR : $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/auth.json . Otherwise, including macOS and Windows: ~/.config/containers/auth.json . For authenticated HTTP sources, set OAUTH2_BEARER in the invoking environment: ogc-records-parquet https://catalog.example.org/records/workflow.json \ --output records.parquet Exit status ¶ 0 : conversion succeeded, or help was displayed. 1 : a source could not be read or parsed, or output could not be written. 2 : invalid command usage, such as missing inputs or --output . Progress and diagnostic logs are written to standard error. A failed write may leave a partial output file; output replacement is not atomic.

docs.text: Errors and limitations ¶ Failure timing ¶ records_to_arrow() validates the projection schema, batch size, and collection metadata immediately. Record conversion is lazy. Consume the reader or write it to detect per-record failures. Generator readers likewise report errors when iterated. Failure Action Invalid or reserved projection name Use a unique non-empty object path; do not name a reserved storage column. Unsafe projection conversion Select a compatible Arrow type or leave the field unprojected. Missing non-nullable projection Supply the field or make the projection nullable. Non-JSON or non-finite value Replace tuples, unsupported Python objects, non-string keys, and NaN/infinity before storage. Duplicate key in stored JSON Correct the source payload; decoding rejects ambiguity. Membership length mismatch Align collection_ids with records before consumption. Invalid membership Use a non-empty string or None . Missing format metadata or payload Retain library metadata and __record_json when filtering/exporting Arrow results. Unsupported format version Use a reader supporting that format; changing the version label alone is not migration. Missing destination directory Create the parent directory before calling to_parquet() . Storage validation failures generally raise ValueError ; JSON syntax errors are json.JSONDecodeError , a ValueError subclass. Filesystem, PyArrow writer, and PySTAC serialization errors can propagate. Error message text is not a versioned interface. Limits ¶ OGC conformance, application profiles, and geometry topology are not validated. The package does not execute queries or translate CQL2. CRS84 inputs are required; reprojection and other input CRSs are not supported. Writes target local files, not remote or object-storage destinations. Batch size counts records; it is not a memory-size guarantee. JSON payload storage duplicates some values held in query columns. Projection schemas are explicit or use the defaults; there is no automatic full-file inference, first-batch inference, or disk-backed schema unification. Raw source JSON bytes and timestamp precision before PySTAC normalization are not preserved. Failed writes ¶ Local writes stage data in the destination directory and replace the target after success. A conversion failure leaves an existing destination unchanged. This behavior is not a transaction spanning multiple files or a remote storage guarantee.

docs.text: Storage format ¶ Versions ¶ Version domain Current behavior Package Defined by ogc_records_parquet.__version__ ; independent of file versions OGC Records storage format records_to_arrow() creates 1.1.0 ; readers accept 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 GeoParquet metadata 1.1.0 Format 1.1.0 declares and stores row membership. Format 1.0.0 has no membership contract; its membership reader returns null for each row. Package 0.1.0 readers reject format 1.1.0 files. to_parquet() preserves a supplied valid legacy schema and version. To create the current format from older records, use the migration procedure . Reserved columns ¶ Name Arrow type Meaning geometry binary, nullable ISO WKB, in CRS84 longitude/latitude coordinates bbox nullable struct of four float64 fields Geometry-derived two-dimensional covering __collection_id string, nullable Storage-only membership; non-empty string or null __record_json large_string, non-nullable Authoritative serialized Record document The bbox field order is xmin , ymin , xmax , ymax . Null and empty geometry have null covering values. An original JSON bbox is retained independently in the payload. The geometry field metadata contains: ARROW:extension:name = geoarrow.wkb . ARROW:extension:metadata , with a JSON-encoded CRS84 definition. There is no reprojection. Inputs must already use CRS84. Query projections ¶ default_schema() returns the following nullable query fields, before storage columns and format metadata are added: Field Arrow type id string type string properties.type string properties.title string properties.description string properties.created string properties.updated string properties.keywords list of string Projection field names select dot-separated paths through objects. Missing paths or paths passing through a non-object produce null. Lists are projected as a whole; list traversal and escaping literal dots in keys are not supported. Names must be unique, non-empty, and have no empty path segments. Reserved column names cannot be supplied as projections. The default id projection is string-valued, including for integer identifiers. The integer remains an integer in the payload. Default timestamp projections are strings containing the extension's normalized values. Other projection values use inferred Arrow types followed by safe casts to the requested field types. Missing/null values in a non-nullable field fail. Unprojected fields remain in the payload. Schema metadata ¶ Existing projection schema metadata is retained except for the library-owned geo and ogc-records-parquet keys, which are replaced. geo ¶ The GeoParquet declaration specifies: Version 1.1.0 and primary column geometry . WKB encoding, planar edges, and CRS84. An empty geometry_types list. Covering paths pointing to the four bbox struct fields. ogc-records-parquet ¶ The JSON object has these fields: Field Meaning version Storage format version writer_version Package version that created the schema payload_column __record_json membership_column __collection_id in format 1.1.0 projections Mapping from projected names to lists of path segments collections Optional mapping of IDs to catalog JSON objects Catalog descriptions do not assign row membership. Unknown membership remains null even if only one catalog description exists. Payload contract ¶ The payload is JSON text from OGCRecord.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) . It preserves the extension's serialized values, includes self links when present, and leaves relative hrefs unchanged. Readers use OGCRecord.from_dict() . Query columns are not used to reconstruct the payload. Whitespace, escape spelling, member order, and pre-PySTAC normalization details are outside the preservation contract.

docs.text: Your first round trip ¶ In this tutorial you will create a record, write it to GeoParquet, recover it, and export an edited JSON document. No external data service is needed. Prepare the environment ¶ Use a local checkout and Python 3.11 or newer. From the repository root: python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e . On Windows, activate the environment with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell instead. Start Python from the repository root. Run the following Python blocks in the same session. Create a record ¶ from pathlib import Path from pystac.extensions.ogc_record import OGCRecord from ogc_records_parquet import read_parquet, records_to_arrow, to_parquet record = OGCRecord( id="flood-mapping", properties={ "type": "service", "title": "Flood mapping", "keywords": ["flood", "mapping"], }, ) original = record.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) assert record.geometry is None The record describes a service. It has no geometry or observation datetime; neither is needed for this storage operation. Write the file ¶ output = Path("tutorial-output") output.mkdir(exist_ok=True) path = output / "records.parquet" reader = records_to_arrow([record], batch_size=128) to_parquet(reader, path) assert path.is_file() reader is a lazy Arrow stream. The writer consumes it and creates the file. Running this step again replaces the destination after a successful write. Recover the record ¶ restored = list(read_parquet(path)) assert len(restored) == 1 assert isinstance(restored[0], OGCRecord) assert restored[0].to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) == original print(restored[0].title) Expected output: Flood mapping The equality compares PySTAC-serialized documents, not the bytes of an original JSON file. Edit and export ¶ restored[0].title = "Updated flood mapping" json_path = output / "updated-record.json" restored[0].save_object(dest_href=str(json_path)) assert OGCRecord.from_file(json_path).title == "Updated flood mapping" assert next(read_parquet(path)).title == "Flood mapping" You now have a Parquet file and an edited JSON file under tutorial-output/ . Editing the recovered object does not modify the stored file. Continue with query projections to select records using Arrow columns, or read why the full document is stored .
